notice: Generated from the code. Do not edit by hand: edit the templates or the situations and regenerate.

rules.pick_by_situation: Choose the template from the situation the beat is for, never from habit or from what the last beat used.
rules.one_region_each: A template owns one region. Two templates may not share a region on the same frame.
rules.type_never_overlaps_type: Every word is masked to its own box; the self-check measures this.
rules.no_shake: No template translates or rotates the camera. Motion is one direction, eased, then still.
rules.beat_length: A template refuses a beat outside its band; pick another template rather than stretching it.

opening-claim.says: Open the film by stating the premise in one sentence.

name-the-thing.says: Put a name or a key figure on the frame so it can be remembered.

state-the-thesis.says: State the idea the rest of the section argues for.

punchline.says: Land a short line at the end of an argument, with nothing else on screen.

explain-a-number.says: Show a figure the script claims, so it can be read rather than guessed.

show-a-sequence.says: Walk through steps in the order the narration reads them.

show-criteria.says: List the conditions something has to meet, one at a time.

make-a-comparison.says: Put two options or two states against each other.

before-and-after.says: Show what the same thing looked like before, and what it looks like now.

show-the-mechanism.says: Reveal how something works by showing the actual commands or code.

show-the-command.says: Put one command on the frame and let it type.

build-an-argument.says: Add one more reason to a stack, so each one is felt as an addition.

recap.says: Bring a section back to a short list of what it said.

hold-a-beat.says: Fill a short pause between two big beats with real motion.

punctuation.says: Mark a change of section with something small and deliberate.

templates.name: Kinetic headline
templates.purpose: Sets one spoken sentence as type that performs itself, word by word, with an optional second row.
avoid: More than twelve words: at that length the arrival outlasts the line.
A beat that also needs a diagram or a list: this template owns its whole region.

templates.name: Count up
templates.purpose: Counts a number the script actually claims, with its label and a rule under it.
avoid: Any figure the script does not state: a counted number is a factual claim.
A beat under a second: the count is unreadable below that.

templates.name: List build
templates.purpose: Builds a list one row at a time, in the order the narration reads it.
avoid: More than four items in a short beat: the rows arrive too fast to read.
A single item: that is a headline, not a list.

templates.name: Compare pair
templates.purpose: Puts two things side by side and draws a divider between them.
avoid: Two long paragraphs: each half fits three short lines at most.
A comparison the script does not make: don't stage an argument nobody said.

templates.name: Code typing
templates.purpose: Types code or commands onto the frame, with a caret.
avoid: Code the film does not show elsewhere: it dates the piece.
Long lines: they are clipped, not wrapped, by design.

templates.name: Bar compare
templates.purpose: Grows bars to their values, so two or three numbers can be read at a glance.
avoid: More than five bars: the labels stop fitting.
Invented data. Every value must come from the script.

templates.name: Sweep rule
templates.purpose: A rule crosses the region with a small label at its head; the beat-filler that is still motion.
avoid: Anything over 1.2 seconds: below that length it is a transition, above it it is a held frame with a line on it.
A beat that carries information: this template says nothing.

templates.name: Stack push
templates.purpose: Stacks labelled slabs, each arrival pushing everything already on screen.
avoid: More than four slabs: the stack runs out of region.
A beat whose items are not parallel in kind.

templates.name: Fork paths
templates.purpose: One thing splitting into two outcomes, drawn as a source and two branches.
avoid: Two things that do not come from the same source: the fork would be a lie.
More than two branches: it becomes spaghetti.

templates.name: Matrix grid
templates.purpose: Two to four things as tiles that fill in the order they are spoken.
avoid: One item: that is a headline, not a grid.
Five or more: the labels stop being readable at a glance.

items: Read the diff, not the summary
Ask what it does not handle

templates.name: Ring gauge
templates.purpose: A claimed number as a dial that sweeps to it, with the unit on the ring.
avoid: A number the narration does not say: the dial would be decoration.
Two numbers on one beat: one dial, one figure.

templates.name: Budget rail
templates.purpose: A span of time divided into the parts the narration says it is spent on.
avoid: Parts that do not sum to the whole being explained.
More than four segments: the labels collide on the rail.

segments.label: Ten seconds asking what it refuses

templates.name: Stamp lockup
templates.purpose: Impresses the closing phrase onto the frame as a stamped object.
avoid: A long sentence: a stamp holds four or five words, not a clause.
Anywhere but the end of an argument: a stamp is a verdict.

templates.name: Command console
templates.purpose: A window that types one command and shows the run finishing, block by block.
avoid: More than one command: the window holds one line.
Code the film does not otherwise mention.

templates.name: Dot gauge
templates.purpose: A proportion as countable marks: the lit dots are the part the narration names.
avoid: A proportion too large to count: over forty marks and the dots read as texture.
Two proportions on one beat: one grid, one part.

templates.name: Timeline rail
templates.purpose: A sequence of moments on one axis, with a marker that arrives where the narration arrives.
avoid: Moments that are not in time order: the rail would be a list in disguise.
More than six stops: the labels collide.

templates.name: Overlap pair
templates.purpose: Two things that share a middle, drawn as two circles whose overlap is hatched.
avoid: Two things with nothing in common: the lens would be empty.
Three or more sets: two circles are the most this picture holds.

templates.name: Exploded stack
templates.purpose: A whole taken apart into the layers it is made of, each labelled as it separates.
avoid: Layers that are not parts of one whole.
More than four layers: the labels run out of room.

entrances.rule: The act picks one entrance from the ones its template can carry, never the one the act before it used.
entrances.source: Canvas 2D ports of the motion basics in howardc38/motion-fx-lab (0BSD).
